correctness.rationale: The exact one-dimensional kernel of the oriented unicyclic incidence map gives the affine image of a bridge cube times a projected cycle cube. Balanced cycle sign vectors maximize projected squared norm, and their uniform distribution combined with independent bridge signs has mean zero and covariance exactly one over d times the claimed ellipsoid shape. The determinant-trace AM–GM inequality therefore proves global enclosing minimality and equality uniqueness, not just an invariant-family optimum. The weighted Laplacian is the image shape, and the matrix-tree pseudodeterminant nk yields exact intrinsic volume. Parity-specific algebra and strict Bernoulli inequality establish the claimed monotone ordering. Independently rerun exact-rational checker passed 51 graph configurations and 6696 sign-pattern tests. No finite search is substituted for the analytical argument.

value.rationale: This is an exact natural metric-geometric invariant for every graph with one cycle, not an arbitrary selected finite slice. A strong structural law emerges: the unique optimal ellipsoid is always a two-weight graph Laplacian, its entire contact orbit is determined by a balanced cycle-sign condition, and its Euclidean volume forgets all bridge-attachment structure despite potentially different graph geometry. The full strict n-fixed cycle-length extremizer theorem identifies triangle-cycle minimizers and the unique pure-cycle maximizer, giving comparison across an infinite family. It is not furnished solely by vertex counting, the matrix-tree theorem, or known general ellipsoid optimality criteria.
